important.name: Open-list absence hides an issue newer than the list, and the age rule blocks the recheck
important.summary:
TASK-4 makes `isClosed` take the fresher known answer from the open list (`open_issues.json`) and the gh cache, and TASK-5 rechecks only issues whose freshest answer is older than `ghMaxAgeHours`. An issue opened after the last `untracked` run, or set in an override after it, is absent from the list, so the list answers CLOSED as of `fetched_at`. That inferred answer is fresh, so TASK-5 skips the gh recheck and the issue stays hidden until the list ages past `todo.gh.max_age_hours` (up to 24 h by default). A PR number stored as an override issue never appears in `gh issue list`, so it stays hidden for good. The spec's anti-goal (an issue is never hidden without a known state) assumes absence means closed, and that does not hold for numbers newer than the list. No planned test covers it: the TASK-4 cases cover a fresher list against an older CLOSED cache entry and the reverse, not an issue missing from an older list.

Also (docs): TASK-4 says 'own refs = own override filtered by visibleRefs, else the plan union unfiltered (D4)'. It does not say whether 'else' fires only when no override exists, or also when the override exists but every ref is hidden. The spec says a segment with every ref hidden is not drawn (design.md:30), which suggests an empty own part, while the 'else' reading would show the plan union instead. The builder (opus) has to pick, and the tests listed for TASK-4 do not pin either reading.

Also (overall): TASK-4 gives own refs as 'own override filtered by visibleRefs, else the plan union unfiltered (D4)'. When an own override exists but every ref is hidden (item retired and issue closed), the action does not say whether the head falls back to the plan union or shows plan links only. Today `override ?? union` (line.ts:41) would keep the empty filtered refs, and the plan names no test for this case.
fix: TASK-4: absence from the open list counts as CLOSED only when the override entry's `set_at` is older than the list's `fetched_at` (an issue set later has no answer from the list), with a line.test/hide.test case for an override set after the list.
TASK-4/TASK-5: let the open list answer only OPEN (presence) and leave CLOSED to the gh cache, and update spec Goals 'Issue state from two feeds' and D2's rationale to match.
TASK-2: `open_issues.json` also records the highest issue number listed, and TASK-4 treats absence as CLOSED only for numbers up to it, with a test for a number above it.

State in TASK-4's action that an own override whose refs are all hidden yields an empty own part (no fallback to the plan union), and add that case to the line.test.ts list; or state the opposite explicitly.

TASK-4: state that a fully hidden own override leaves the head with the plan links only (no fallback, matching 'an override replaces the plan refs'), or that it falls back to the plan union, and add a line.test case for the chosen behavior.

important.name: Overlapping gh recheck passes break the once-per-age bound
important.summary:
TASK-5 schedules a recheck with `later` after every scan. Scans come close together at session start, on the snapshot write, at the first prompt and after a tool call (watch.ts:372, 381, 393, 399). Each recheck reads `issues.json`, calls gh for every stale issue and writes the cache once at its end. Nothing marks a pass as in flight: `pacing.isBusy` (watch.ts:307-316) serializes scans but not the rechecks they queue, so two passes started before the first one writes run the same `gh issue view` calls and race on `issues.json`. With gh missing, each call waits up to `GIT_TIMEOUT_MS` (10 s), so the overlap is likely. Spec anti-goals limit checks to 'at most once per issue per `todo.gh.max_age_hours`', and the planned test 'one gh call per stale issue' covers only a single pass.

Also (overall): TASK-5 runs `gh issue view <n> --json state`, adding `--repo` only when `ghRepo` is set, and `todo.gh.repo` defaults to null (defaults.json:88). Every process the mod runs today pins the checkout with `git -C root` (watch.ts:175), and no mod passes a working directory to `$.process.run`. gh has no `-C`, so with a null repo it resolves the repository from the host process's working directory, not from `w.root`. The Python side runs gh with `cwd=project_root` (todo_sync/gh.py:31), so the two feeds can answer for different repositories. A session started outside the project, or a worktree of another clone, would then check, cache and hide issues from the wrong repository.

Also (overall): TASK-5 drops the `branch === null` guard (watch.ts:297) and writes `{version: 1, branch, text}`. Before git-status writes its first snapshot, `branch` is null. TASK-7's widget prints the stamped branch dark plus ` · ` whenever it differs from HEAD, so a null branch (or a '' text from 'text '' for no line') prints `null · ` or a bare dark branch with a trailing separator. Neither task says what the stamp holds or what the widget prints in these cases, and none of the five planned widget tests covers them. Without a snapshot, `buildLine('')` also labels the current branch's own override as another branch (`[ <current> refs ]`) until the snapshot scan runs.
fix: TASK-5: hold a module-level recheck guard (a busy flag, or a set of issue numbers in flight) so a recheck requested while one runs is skipped or owed, as `pacing` does for scans; add a watch.test case where two scans in a row produce one gh call per stale issue.

TASK-5: when `ghRepo` is null, resolve `owner/name` once per session from `git -C <root> remote get-url origin` and pass it as `--repo`; skip the recheck, leaving the state unknown, when that fails. Add a watch.test case asserting the `--repo` argument.
TASK-5: run gh with the project root as its working directory, if the engine's `process.run` accepts one, and say so in the action with a test that asserts it.

TASK-5: write `branch` as null when no snapshot exists. TASK-7: the widget prints nothing when `text` is empty and prints `text` without a stamp when `branch` is not a non-empty string. Add both cases to the planned test_setup_statusline_contract.py.
TASK-5: skip writing line.json and line.txt until the first snapshot gives a branch, and say so in the action and README.

important.name: TASK-7 planned red ImportError stops holding once its own dependency TASK-2 is recorded

Move the LINE_JSON_REL addition from TASK-2 into TASK-7 (and the TASK-3 contract test's dependency accordingly), so ImportError stays the true red until TASK-7 itself lands.

minor.name: Deferred research reads plan links back from line.json, which holds only rendered text
minor.summary:

The spec (design.md:35-37) and plan TASK-5 (ActionPlan.json:258) fix line.json as {version, branch, text}, with text the ANSI statusText form; it holds no structured plan links, only OSC 8 escapes inside a string. The recorded 'smallest change' therefore needs either a new line.json field or parsing escapes, which the note does not say.

Also (overall): plan-link-stale-paint.md step 2 carries over 'each plan link it holds' from the previous line.json. TASK-5 writes line.json as `{version, branch, text}`, where `text` is the ccstatusline form with OSC 8 escapes, so it holds no structured plan links to carry over without parsing the escapes.
fix: Reword step 2 to state that line.json gains a `plans` field ([{id, page}]) written beside `text` (a line.json version bump), and that the carry-over reads that field.
Or name a separate mod-owned file for the carried links and drop the 'no new store' claim.
Say in step 2 that line.json would gain a `plans` field (id and page) for the carry-over, or carry the links from the `line` atom (WorkingLine.plans) instead.

minor.name: Length cap does not count the ccstatusline branch stamp
minor.summary: The spec says the line stops at max_chars total (design.md:24-26) and D5 sizes 120 to one status line. TASK-4 measures the cap on the plain text only, and TASK-7 prepends '<branch> · ' in the widget when the stamped branch differs, outside the cap, so the printed ccstatusline line can exceed max_chars by a branch name plus three characters.
fix: State in the spec Goals that max_chars caps the line the mod builds and that the widget's branch stamp is added on top; or have TASK-7 note the overflow as accepted.

minor.name: 'Spawns no process' contradicts the widget, which is a node process per repaint
minor.summary: The spec anti-goal (design.md:51) rules out 'a status-line command that spawns a process on every repaint', and TASK-7 (ActionPlan.json:333) says 'no process is spawned'. The widget is itself `node -e ...` (ccstatusline.defaults.json:33), launched by ccstatusline on every repaint, and the planned tests run it that way. The intended rule is that the command starts no further child process (no git call) and reads files only.
fix: Reword design.md:51 to 'A status-line command that runs git or another child process on every repaint: the widget's node one-liner reads files only.' and TASK-7's 'no process is spawned' to 'it starts no child process (no git call)'.
